title: Personal Breadth widget -- non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #171 (frontend-breadth-widget), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: PersonalBreadthCard.tsx's unavailable-count footnote ('N of M tracked ticker(s) currently unavailable') pluralizes 'ticker(s)' based on unavailable_count instead of the total tracked_ticker_count it's actually attached to -- e.g. unavailable_count=1 with tracked_ticker_count=5 renders 'ticker' instead of 'tickers'. Locked in verbatim by PersonalBreadthCard.test.tsx's assertion of the exact (grammatically wrong) string, so fixing it needs the test's expected string updated too.

personalBreadthHelp.ts's unavailableClause has the identical pluralization bug ('N of M tracked ticker(s) unavailable right now') -- pluralizes on unavailableCount rather than trackedTickerCount, inconsistent with the correct pattern two lines later in the same function (the computable-ticker clause correctly pluralizes off the total, computable).

personalBreadthHelp.ts's valueInterpretation sentence always uses the plural verb 'are' even when the computable-ticker count is singular (e.g. computable=1 renders '1 of 1 computable ticker (100.0%) are currently BULLISH' -- should be 'is'). Also locked in verbatim by PersonalBreadthCard.test.tsx's singular-wording test.

New from PR #171's re-review (PersonalBreadthCard.tsx fix commit 2acf19c): the 'is'/'are' fix above keys the verb off `computable` (the computable-ticker denominator) instead of `bullishCount` (the actual grammatical subject of "...are currently BULLISH"), so it's still wrong whenever those two differ -- e.g. tracked_ticker_count=5, unavailable_count=1, bullish_count=1, bearish_count=3, neutral_count=0 gives computable=4, so the code emits 'are' ('1 of 4 computable tickers (25.0%) are currently BULLISH'), which should be 'is' since only 1 ticker is BULLISH. Also wrong when bullish_count=0 and computable=1 (emits 'is' for a zero count, which conventionally takes 'are'). The only test covering this fix (computable=1 AND bullishCount=1) can't distinguish the two variables, so the residual bug ships uncovered. Fix: key the is/are ternary off `bullishCount === 1`, not `computable === 1`.

decisions.decision: Fixed all three grammar findings directly on task/frontend-breadth-widget (PR #171) alongside the blocking alignItems fix, rather than waiting for a dedicated followups branch/PR for this task id.
decisions.rationale: The dispatching instruction explicitly called these 'cheap to bundle now' while already in these exact files for the blocking fix, and all three are one-line ternary-condition changes with no new design surface. Rejected alternative: leaving them for a separate task/frontend-breadth-widget-followups branch later, which would mean re-opening and re-verifying (tsc -b, full test suite, eslint) the same two files a second time for no benefit. State intentionally left as 'planned' (not 'done') despite the checklist being fully checked off -- closing a task's lifecycle to 'done' is pr-reviewer's/task-qa-reviewer's call per CLAUDE.md's mover convention, not task-worker's, even for a followups task whose fix happened to land as a drive-by; pr-reviewer can confirm and close this out on its next pass over PR #171.

decisions.decision: Fixed the residual is/are bug on its own task/frontend-breadth-widget-followups branch (this task's own branch), keying personalBreadthHelp.ts's valueInterpretation ternary off `bullishCount === 1` instead of `computable === 1`. Added two new tests to PersonalBreadthCard.test.tsx that each set bullishCount and computable to different values (bullish_count=1 with computable=4, and bullish_count=0 with computable=1) so the is/are wording is actually exercised independently of the computable-ticker count, rather than adding a dedicated unit-test file for personalBreadthHelp.ts directly.
decisions.rationale: Unlike the first three findings (bundled into #171 because that branch was still open), this fourth finding was raised only after #171 already merged, so there was no still-open branch to bundle it into -- a fresh task/<id> branch per CLAUDE.md's normal task-worker flow is the right unit of work here. Kept the new tests inside PersonalBreadthCard.test.tsx (component-level, via MetricHelp's rendered text) rather than adding a standalone personalBreadthHelp.test.ts, matching the existing pattern for this exact help-content style (features/portfolio/components/totalRiskHelp.ts has no dedicated unit test file either, only exercised through its card's tests) -- rejected alternative: a new isolated unit test file, which would be more direct but inconsistent with the sibling pattern and unnecessary duplication of the MSW-mocked rendering path already in place here.

review.notes: Full review: backend pytest (746 passed, 99.92% cov) and frontend vitest (536 passed, statements 99.55%/branches 98.66%) both pass well above the 90% gate; no coverage regression. ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc -b --noEmit all clean on both sides. code-review skill (medium effort) found zero issues. Hand-checked the fixed ternary (`bullishCount === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'`) against bullishCount=0/1/>1 crossed with computable equal-to and different-from bullishCount -- correct ('is' only for exactly one BULLISH ticker, 'are' otherwise, independent of the computable denominator) in every case, matching docs/Analyse.md's plain-English framing (no methodology rule at stake, this is presentation text). Mentally reverted the fix (restoring `computable === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'`) against both new tests: the computable=4/bullishCount=1 test would flip to 'are' (wrong, test expects 'is') and the computable=1/bullishCount=0 test would flip to 'is' (wrong, test expects 'are') -- both new tests genuinely catch the original bug. `gh pr diff --name-only` confirms only the two watchlist frontend files plus the two task-board JSON files changed -- no backend/API/schema touched, so no openapi.json regeneration was needed. No new module/component/dependency added (architecture-review and the components/common/-vs-feature placement check in step 7a don't apply here -- personalBreadthHelp.ts and PersonalBreadthCard.test.tsx are pre-existing files being edited, not new components). Browser walkthrough: started backend (fixture provider) + frontend dev servers, drove the Watchlist page with a real Chromium browser (not just RTL) -- added 3 tickers then removed down to 1, opening the Personal Breadth help popover at each step; live-rendered text read '0 of 3 computable tickers (0.0%) are currently BULLISH...' and '0 of 1 computable ticker (0.0%) are currently BULLISH...', correctly using 'are' for a zero bullish count independent of the computable denominator (3 vs 1) -- confirms the fix works end to end, not just in the mocked unit tests. Fixture data never produced a bullish_count of 1 to observe the 'is' branch live, but that combination is already covered by the new component tests plus my hand-check above. Two console 404s appeared only from my own test script's cleanup DELETE calls firing after the page had already navigated away -- not an application bug. e2e-test skill: `make e2e` ran all 4 spec files / 16 tests, all passed, no console errors. No checklist item here is phrased as 'decide X' needing a decisions entry beyond the two already recorded, both of which have proper rationale. No non-blocking findings -- nothing to file as a follow-up task.
